c11_acc_cbse_06_003: Whether an error shows in the Trial Balance depends on it being one- or two-sided, not its name — a wrong-account posting with right amounts still tallies.
c12_acc_cbse_06_004: Collateral debentures are recorded at their full face value issued, not the loan amount — the extra margin is a safety cushion for the lender.
c11_acc_cbse_06_004: Wrong account isn't always commission — machinery in the Purchases Book breaks a principle (capital vs revenue), making it an error of principle.
c12_acc_cbse_06_005: Debenture interest is always on face value, not issue price — a 9% debenture pays 9% of ₹100 even if issued at ₹95. Check the nominal value.
c11_acc_cbse_06_005: Complete omission leaves both sides missing, so the Trial Balance still tallies — only partial omission breaks it. Check whether one side got posted.
c12_acc_cbse_06_006: Loss on issue isn't just the discount — if debentures are redeemable at a premium, add that premium too. Look at cash out at redemption, not just at issue.
c11_acc_cbse_06_006: A posting error doesn't always break the Trial Balance — if the wrong amount sits in the original book, both sides get it equally. Check one-sided vs two-sided.
c12_acc_cbse_06_007: Draw of lots redeems only the drawn debentures — the rest stay a live liability. Debit Debentures for just the drawn amount; no provision for the remainder.
c11_acc_cbse_06_007: Compensating errors happen in different accounts — an excess debit offset by a short debit elsewhere. Same-account offsets are just two errors, not a pair.
c12_acc_cbse_06_008: Own debentures aren't an investment to keep — cancel them immediately. And profit on cancellation is capital, not interest income to P&L.
c11_acc_cbse_06_008: Suspense Account is only for one-sided errors that break the Trial Balance — two-sided errors are fixed by a direct journal entry between the accounts.
c12_acc_cbse_06_009: DRR is a reserve (appropriated profit, no asset); a sinking fund is reserve plus actual investments. And the 15% applies to debentures maturing next year only.
c11_acc_cbse_06_009: Suspense Account isn't a universal fixer — it only absorbs net differences from one-sided errors. Two-sided errors get a normal correcting entry.
c12_acc_cbse_06_010: Premium on redemption is a liability the company owes at maturity — credit it at issue, debit it at redemption. It's not a capital profit like securities premium.
c11_acc_cbse_06_010: P&L Adjustment is only for nominal account errors — a missed machinery purchase still gets Machinery Dr. to Creditor Cr. Check the account class first.
c12_acc_cbse_07_001: Company financials aren't just two statements — Schedule III mandates format, cash flow statement, equity changes and notes. It's law, not a template.
c11_acc_cbse_07_001: Depreciation allocates original cost over useful periods — it isn't a market-value adjustment. A machine depreciates even if its market price rises.
c12_acc_cbse_07_002: Schedule III order is law, not suggestion — wrong classification breaks comparability and ratios and can attract penalties. Check the prescribed heads.
c11_acc_cbse_07_002: Depreciation isn't only physical wear — obsolescence and expired legal rights count too. A working computer can still be depreciating.
c12_acc_cbse_07_003: The Statement of P&L isn't the old T-format — Schedule III prescribes specific expense sub-heads and separates exceptional items. Follow the legal format.
c11_acc_cbse_07_003: Cost includes freight, installation and trial runs — and residual value is net of disposal costs. Check both before computing depreciable amount.
c12_acc_cbse_07_004: Calls in Arrears reduces subscribed capital — it isn't a receivable. And it never nets against Calls in Advance, which is a current liability.
c11_acc_cbse_07_004: Under SLM the rate applies to (cost − scrap), not raw original cost — derive the rate from the depreciable amount, then apply it.
c12_acc_cbse_07_005: Unclaimed dividend is a certain liability → Other Current Liabilities, not a provision. Forfeited shares sit under Share Capital, not Reserves.
c11_acc_cbse_07_005: Under WDV the base shrinks every year — apply the rate to the written-down value, not original cost. Year 2's charge is smaller than Year 1's.
c12_acc_cbse_07_006: Under Schedule III, share capital shows nominal value — issue discount goes to Other Non-Current Assets (or is written off), not netted under Share Capital.
c11_acc_cbse_07_006: WDV isn't automatically 'better' because tax law uses it — books can use SLM, some assets need SLM, and WDV never reaches zero. Weigh all the factors.
c12_acc_cbse_07_007: Classify by purpose, not looks: breeding livestock is PPE (inventory only for a trader); loose tools are consumables, not fixed assets.
